examples.title: Keep both CSV schemas and retain file provenance
examples.sql:
SELECT id::INTEGER AS id, amount_text, coupon,
  parse_filename(filename) AS source_file
FROM read_csv(['schema-early.csv','schema-later.csv'],
  union_by_name = true, all_varchar = true)
ORDER BY id;

examples.title: Combine the Parquet equivalents with a deliberate amount type
examples.sql:
SELECT id, try_cast(amount_text AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS amount,
  coupon, parse_filename(filename) AS source_file
FROM read_parquet(['schema-early.parquet','schema-later.parquet'], union_by_name = true)
ORDER BY id;

examples.title: Keep the original value beside the conversion decision
examples.sql:
SELECT id::INTEGER AS id, amount_text,
  try_cast(amount_text AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS amount,
  CASE WHEN amount_text IS NULL THEN 'missing'
    WHEN try_cast(amount_text AS DECIMAL(10,2)) IS NULL THEN 'review'
    ELSE 'accepted' END AS amount_status
FROM read_csv(['schema-early.csv','schema-later.csv'],
  union_by_name = true, all_varchar = true)
ORDER BY id;

challenge.title: Find values that failed numeric conversion
challenge.prompt: Return id and amount_text only for non-NULL source amounts that cannot become DECIMAL(10,2). Read both CSV files.
challenge.hint: Use TRY_CAST to test conversion, and keep the original text for diagnosis.
challenge.starter: SELECT id::INTEGER AS id, amount_text FROM read_csv(['schema-early.csv','schema-later.csv'], union_by_name=true, all_varchar=true) ORDER BY id;
challenge.solution: SELECT id::INTEGER AS id, amount_text FROM read_csv(['schema-early.csv','schema-later.csv'], union_by_name=true, all_varchar=true) WHERE amount_text IS NOT NULL AND try_cast(amount_text AS DECIMAL(10,2)) IS NULL ORDER BY id;
challenge.success: ID 4 needs review. Adding a column is a schema problem; pending in a numeric field is a value problem.
